evidence_items.publisher: The New York Times, reproduced on NowComment
evidence_items.explanation: The contemporaneous report supports rapid, repeated production of fluent false content. Its own repeat experiment elicited disinformation on 33 percent of sampled questions, but it supplies no matched fluency comparison with GPT-2.

evidence_items.locator: Opening results section, paragraph beginning 'The results confirm fears'
evidence_items.explanation: This original audit demonstrates repeated fabricated-content generation shortly before the target period. Some narratives required up to five attempts, and the audit did not compare fluency with GPT-2 or measure industrial throughput.

evidence_items.locator: Appendix B, Experiments with Larger Models
evidence_items.explanation: This earlier comparison cautions against assuming a large improvement on every writing-quality proxy. It measured detection of the boundary between human and generated text, not hoax-article fluency, and the authors say the task may need much more data to distinguish strong models.

unresolved_gaps: No sufficiently comparable evaluation located establishes the claimed substantial fluency improvement between GPT-2 and the newest models available during the target period on fabricated-article writing.
